subject: Hybrid VLAN segmentation / IaC review for Acme private deployment
messages:
From: Danielle Ross <danielle@acme-corp.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Networking Team <netops@acme-corp.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Hybrid VLAN segmentation design and IaC review request

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for yesterday's call. As discussed, Acme is moving forward with a private deployment in our us-west-2 VPC but with on-prem tie-ins for legacy services. We need a concise review from Redwood on our proposed hybrid VLAN segmentation pattern and the accompanying IaC (Terraform + Helm + Ansible) before the security committee meeting next week.

High-level asks:
- Confirm the Terraform modules isolate tenant-specific routes (vlan routing + route tables) and do not expose control-plane ports to customer networks.
- Validate the Helm values for the edge NGINX proxies and that we have the correct liveness/readiness policies to avoid noisy restarts.
- Quick sanity check on the Ansible playbook that runs the on-prem configuration push (should be idempotent and safe for partial failures).

I've attached a current network diagram and a small patch with our Terraform changes. The team is expecting feedback on scope and any non-blocking recommendations.

Attachments: [Attachment: network-diagram-v2.png (png, 450KB)], [Attachment: tf-modules-diff.patch (text, 18KB)]

Thanks,
Danielle
Principal Cloud Architect
Acme Corp

Hi Danielle — thanks for the materials, just pulled them down. Marcus and Irene are looped in for infra and ops checks. Quick notes up front:

- We'll run the Terraform through a module-safety pass (checking outputs, remote state locking, and provider pinning).
- Marcus will look specifically at the route table / next-hop choices for the VLAN breakouts (we want explicit NAT gateways only where needed).
- Irene will validate Ansible idempotency and suggest a safe backout path for on-prem pushes.

Can we do an internal 30-min call Monday to go over the diff and the diagram? I'll prepare an annotated doc with suggested module boundaries and an interim canary plan.

I'll upload a notes doc and a proposed helm-values override for the edge proxies.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan

Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Danielle Ross <danielle@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hybrid VLAN segmentation design and IaC review request

Quick pass from my end after running the Terraform diff locally: 

1) Module boundaries
- The new modules look fine conceptually, but the vlan-module currently exposes a single variable for "allowed_control_cidrs" which is too broad. Suggest split into control_plane_ips and mgmt_plane_ips and document intended consumers.

2) Route propagation
- You're using a shared route table for the on-prem tunnels; recommend dedicated route tables per tenant plus explicit route propagation rules. This reduces blast radius and makes ACL auditing cleaner.

3) Remote state and locking
- The backend configuration has state encryption enabled but missing an explicit locking mechanism for Terraform Cloud/remote state (we flagged similar issues in NETOPS-4018). Add a lock table or enable TFC run-only access for the run account.

4) NACLs vs SGs
- NACLs are currently permissive for ephemeral ports. Convert critical control-plane subnets to deny-by-default with explicit allow entries for management hosts.

I'm attaching a small patch with variable renames and a suggested provider pin list.

Marcus
Senior Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: tf-modules-diff.patch (text, 18KB)]

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Danielle Ross <danielle@acme-corp.com>
Date: Sat, 01 May 2027 10:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hybrid VLAN segmentation design and IaC review request

Thanks — added my Ansible review below. I pulled the playbook that runs the on-prem config push (site-onprem.yml).

- Idempotency: Most tasks use check mode-safe modules, but there are raw shell invocations for vendor firmware steps. Wrap those with a when: not firmware_present checks and register results so we can gate retries.
- Partial failure: Add a transactional marker file on the host (/var/run/redwood-deploy-marker) so we can detect partial runs and have a targeted rollback playbook.
- Secrets handling: The playbook references credentials from a local vault file. Recommend switching to a Transit-backed fetch from your KMS/HSM or using HashiCorp Vault with short-lived tokens — avoiding static files for on-prem access.

Operational suggestion: Include a --dry-run job in the Helm CI pipeline that runs against a namespaced staging cluster that mirrors the edge labels. That is low cost and catches most liveness readiness churn.

Irene
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Danielle Ross <danielle@acme-corp.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 08:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hybrid VLAN segmentation design and IaC review request

Appreciate the thorough pass. A few follow-ups: 
- We'll split the control CIDRs into the two variables you suggested and push a new patch (NETOPS-4127).
- For remote state locking, we can enable DynamoDB-based locks in front of S3 and provide the table name.
- For Ansible, we have an on-prem vault appliance but it only supports long-lived tokens today. We're evaluating HashiCorp Vault for short-lived creds — can you share any runbooks you've used for Vault integration?

I'll upload the updated Terraform patch and the Helm override to the Drive folder by EOD. Also, can you confirm whether Redwood recommends a staged canary that starts with a single tenant (Tenant-A) then broadens to two-tenants before full roll? We want an SLO-friendly plan.

Thanks,
Danielle

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Ross <danielle@acme-corp.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hybrid VLAN segmentation design and IaC review request

Danielle — yes, that staged canary is exactly what we recommend. Proposed immediate action items: 

1) Acme: push the split-variable patch + new tf backend lock config to the Drive folder (NETOPS-4127).
2) Redwood: Marcus will submit a small PR with the provider pins and NACL deny-by-default patch.
3) Redwood: Irene will draft a short Vault-integration runbook and a rollback playbook for on-prem partial failures.
4) Schedule: 30-min joint runbook/rollout sync on Wednesday 10:00am PT. I'll create a calendar invite and attach a deck with the canary gating: success criteria (error-rate <1% and lat p95 < 300ms for 30m window) and automatic rollback thresholds.

I'll also add a short list of Helm probe tuning recommendations in the Drive notes. If that timeline works, we'll treat this as low-risk (canary then two-tenant expansion) and aim for a full roll three days after the two-tenant pass.

Cheers,
Priya
Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
